essence: Sāṅkhya stated at full strength: pradhāna proved by presence, purposed by denying self-aims; change easy; only striving moves; nature faces down (vv19-22).
The page turns on admitted karma: where is His business? Let His triggering be conceived; seed imaged; Sāṅkhya godless; conditional close (vv23-27).

sections.SUMMARY: Sāṅkhya's pradhāna is proved by presence, purposed to spirit by denying self-aims; change comes easy again and again for enjoyment. Only person-aim-striving moves ever-maturing primal stuff; own-nature faces downward from root-cause-seeing toward body's ordaining. Karma admitted as possible mover — then the page turns: where is Īśvara's business? Let His change-triggering be conceived for root-nature's rangers. Seed-kitchens need nothing else, as in sprouts. Three-natured pradhāna leaves Sāṅkhya godless. Puruṣārtha-natured acts are conceived efficient by pradhāna.

rasa.sthayibhava: utsāha (exultation) as Sāṅkhya is stated fairly then outflanked by a question
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is exultation: the opponent at full strength, then the page turning on one question — where is His business? The vyabhicāri is admiration for fairness before victory. Debate relished.
